newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark's EMU opt-out could freeze rating - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Denmark's EMU opt-out could freeze rating - S&P.

text.p: Denmark's 1993 rejection of Economic and Monetary Union could hold it back when ratings agency Standard and Poor's reviews EU states in the light of scheduled monetary union, an S&P executive said on Wednesday.
Denmark's present rating of AA+ is not in question, but its EMU opt-out makes doubtful a rise to AAA that it otherwise might have expected, S&P director Helena Hessel told Reuters.

"The outlook for the Danish economy is stable, with positive indicators and tendencies but as we are at the moment asessing the implications of EMU, Denmark's rating will probably remain unchanged," she said in a telephone interview from New York.
"Denmark's decision not to a be a part of the Euro (currency) from the planned start in January 1999 does not bring its rating down, it's more a question of hindering an upgrade," Hessel added.
After rejecting the Maastricht treaty in a 1992 referendum Danish voters approved it in a fresh plebiscite the following year, on condition that it stay out of EMU.
A fresh referendum, not seen as likely in time to meet the EMU start deadline, would be required in order to reverse the 1993 opt-out. --Per Bech Thomsen, Copenhagen newsroom + 45 33969656
